answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making influence path-dependent. Each new identity is planted in a reputation grove with zero voting weight; only a continuous, time-stamped thread of independently attested useful work, paid from locked stake, can thicken that weight. A sudden gale of cheap wallets cannot seize governance, because scoring credits only countersignatures from already-settled agents after a delay, and any identity that breaks or forks its thread forfeits accumulated influence. Counterfeits therefore spend real time and capital before they matter.
